candidate.answerReason: In the standard ideal elliptical planetary-orbit model, the Sun is at one focus. This placement is a physical modeling fact and cannot be deduced from the definition of an ellipse alone.

methods.label: Elliptical-orbit model
methods.explanation: In the usual ideal model of a planet's elliptical orbit, the Sun is placed at one focus. The sum of distances to the two foci is constant by the definition of an ellipse; the Sun's focal placement is an additional physical modeling fact. Thus the answer is D, at one focus.
methods.levelReason: Recognizing the stipulated orbital model requires no mechanics or advanced mathematics.
